signals.title: NZD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: CHF gained +1.101% across 6 pairs while NZD lost -0.534% across 4 pairs, creating a critical 1.635% G10 spread that anchors downside momentum into Sunday's open. Persistent NZD data misses (ESI -15.0) diverge sharply from strong Swiss outperformance (ESI +20.1), overriding the 275bp nominal carry disadvantage against the franc. Switzerland GDP and KOF Barometer at 08:00 UTC Monday resolve whether CHF outperformance extends through European trading. Trade bias: Short NZD/CHF into the Sydney open. Catalyst: Swiss GDP release at 08:00 UTC Monday. Risk: A rebound above the descending moving averages or an upside NZD data surprise invalidates the breakdown.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short Positioning + Rate Hike Bets
signals.text: EUR COT LF short -105.9k contracts (pctl 2, z=-1.68) sets up elevated short-squeeze risk after Friday closed at 1.0939. Solid U.S. Treasury yields and firming bets on a December Fed hike maintain downside pressure, reinforced by a +151bp OIS carry advantage favoring the dollar. German CPI data at 13:00 UTC Monday followed by ECB President Lagarde's speeches will dictate whether EUR shorts face liquidation. Trade bias: Neutral with an upside squeeze bias on EUR/USD. Catalyst: German CPI and Lagarde speech at 14:30 UTC Monday. Risk: A break below technical support near 1.0900 accelerates trend continuation lower.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Bear Steepener vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 159.51 as U.S. 10Y yields pushed to 4.94% in a classic bear steepener regime (+32.6bp 2s10s). Options markets reflect heavy downside hedging demand with 25-delta risk reversals at -1.77, running directly counter to JPY leveraged funds short positioning of -29.5k. Japan Retail Sales and Industrial Production at 23:50 UTC determine whether Tokyo traders fade the yield-driven rally back below 159.00. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY on the yield spread momentum. Catalyst: Japan Industrial Production at 23:50 UTC Sunday. Risk: Options put skew materializes via BoJ tightening expectations, pushing spot below 158.30.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Crowded Short Base Ahead of Q3 GDP
signals.text: CAD COT LF short -75.4k contracts (22.5% long) keeps USD/CAD supported after closing Friday at 1.4248 above its 20-day SMA of 1.4207. A +141bp OIS carry spread (SOFR 3.95% vs CORRA 2.54%) favors the greenback despite crude oil stabilizing above $83/bbl. Canada Q3 GDP at 13:30 UTC Monday tests whether the Bank of Canada retains room for further tightening. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD into the New York session. Catalyst: Canada Q3 GDP release at 13:30 UTC Monday. Risk: Canada GDP beats the 0.8% annualized forecast, triggering an unwind of CAD net shorts.
